sentences.text: Yuezhuornis is an extinct basal avialan known from a partial skeleton and skull recovered from the Late Jurassic Nanyuan Formation in China.
The holotype specimen is estimated to have weighed about 821 g, based on the width of its femur.
Its humerus is shorter than the femur, a proportion otherwise seen only in a few early birds such as some anchiornithids and the flightless Patagopteryx.
The foot lacks the arctometatarsalian condition, a trait typical of early avialans rather than of dromaeosaurids or troodontids.
The second toe ends in a hyperextensible digit, a feature comparable to that of troodontids and dromaeosaurids.
Yuezhuornis had markedly shorter arms than its closest relatives, indicating it could not fly.
Xu Liming and colleagues formally described Yuezhuornis yangyuanensis as a new genus and species in 2026, designating a specimen as the holotype.
Bone histology shows the individual was close to skeletal maturity, representing a subadult or adult stage.
Yuezhuornis is considered a close relative of Zhengheornis, which comes from the same locality.
The fossil range of Yuezhuornis extends from the Late Jurassic Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian ages.
